newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ March terms of trade show net import price fall.
newsitem.headline: NZ March terms of trade show net import price fall.

text.p: New Zealand's terms of trade rose by 0.4 percent from the December 1996 quarter to the March 1997 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
SNZ said the rise in the terms of trade in the March quarter was the result of a 1.1 percent fall in import prices combined with a 0.7 percent fall in export prices.
"The terms of trade index is now 2.0 percent lower than in the March 1996 quarter, however, compared with the average level during the 1980s the terms of trade are now 8.0 percent higher," SNZ said.

Contributing to the fall in export prices in the latest quarter were wool down 5.6 percent, forestry products down 4.7 percent, dairy products down 3.9 percent, fish down 1.4 percent and chemicals and related products down 0.1 percent.
SNZ said the prices for these exports had weakened throughout the year ended March 1997.
In the latest quarter, price increases were recorded for machinery and transport equipment, meat and aluminium.
Export volumes fell by 4.2 percent during the quarter.
"The seasonal upswing in meat volumes was offset by larger than usual falls in the volumes of forestry products and non- food manufactured goods," SNZ said.

From the March 1996 to the March 1997 quarter, export volumes rose by 5.1 percent, with dairy products up 30.1 percent, aluminium up 14.3 percent, chemicals and related products up 14.1 percent, machinery and transport equipment up 9.0 percent, and forestry products up 1.1 percent.

"Import prices fell for the sixth consecutive quarter and are now 4.6 percent lower than in the March 1996 quarter," SNZ said. Contributing to the latest 1.1 percent fall in import prices were electrical machinery and apparatus down 5.7 percent, textiles down 5.0 percent, food and beverages down 4.9 percent, transport equipment down 2.2 percent and non-electrical machinery down 0.8 percent.
"The only major import commodities to record a price rise in the latest quarter were petroleum up by 10.5 percent and alumina up by 5.0 percent," SNZ said.
Import volumes fell 9.8 percent in the March 1997 quarter but were 1.7 percent higher than in the March 1996 quarter.
Consumption, intermediate and capital goods all contributed to the quarterly decrease in import volumes.
SNZ said on a trade-Weighted basis, the New Zaland dollar appreciated by 1.9 pecent in the quarter and was now 6.5 percent higher than the March 1996 quarter.
